chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left behind his wife while she was pregnant, and she gave birth to a male child after his death. Then the male child died after he hit the ground. The woman who accepted her (as a witness) testified that he cried out and bawled when he hit the ground, and then he died after that. He said: 'It is upon the Imam to validate her testimony regarding one-quarter of the male child's inheritance.'

key_terms.اِسْتَهَلَّ: To cry out or bawl at birth, indicating life

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's testimony regarding an infant's cry for inheritance purposes?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the evidentiary standard for inheritance by accepting a woman's testimony that the infant cried (*istihlal*) upon birth, thereby confirming his status as an heir. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on practical evidence (*shahada*) in establishing lineage and inheritance rights, specifically allocating one-quarter of the infant's estate to the mother as her share. The hadith underscores the flexibility in accepting female testimony in financial matters when corroborating the vital signs of the deceased.
